widgets_values:
Exercise: monocular visual odometry on a real video, scored against ground truth

THE POSES SHIP WITH THE PACK; THE CLIP DOES NOT.
  - kitti_2011_09_26_drive_0009_poses.txt is in example_inputs/ and 'CV Install
    Example Inputs' (workflow 01) copies it into ComfyUI/input for you. It is the
    metric ground truth: one line per frame, the 12 numbers of a 3x4 row-major
    camera-to-world matrix, first frame at the origin.
    WHERE IT COMES FROM: not from a download. KITTI raw ships oxts/data/*.txt -
    GPS/IMU packets - while poses.txt is the separate KITTI *odometry* benchmark's
    format, and that benchmark uses different sequences. This file was DERIVED from
    this drive's oxts log: lat/lon through a Mercator projection to local metres, R
    from roll/pitch/yaw, the first frame as the origin, then composed through
    calib_imu_to_velo and calib_velo_to_cam (from 2011_09_26_calib.zip) so the track
    is the CAMERA centre and not the IMU - the ~0.8 m lever arm rotates during turns,
    so an uncorrected IMU track is not a rigid offset and no alignment absorbs it.
    LICENCE: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, NON-COMMERCIAL, inherited from KITTI - see the 'Data
    sources' note beside this one. It is the one non-commercial file in the pack.
  - kitti_2011_09_26_drive_0009.mp4 is 48 MB, so it stays out of the repo. Build it
    once from 2011_09_26_drive_0009_sync.zip (linked in the 'Data sources' note):
    take image_00/data/*.png - the rectified left grayscale camera - and encode them
    at 10 fps, in filename order. PAD to an even height, never crop or rescale: the
    frames are 1242x375 and any resampling invalidates the camera matrix below. Drop
    the result into ComfyUI/input next to the poses file.
The camera matrix is already filled in here (fx=fy=721.5377, cx=609.5593, cy=172.854); it is P_rect_00 from calib_cam_to_cam.txt in the same calib zip.
Both files are looked up BY NAME in ComfyUI/input, which the graph asks for at run time ('input dir' -> 'join') instead of hard-coding. A plain relative path would be read against whatever folder the SERVER was started from - for the portable build that is the folder above ComfyUI, and nothing ever chdirs - so the load comes back empty and it surfaces one node later as 'Parse Matrix: No matrix data found in the input text'.

WHAT RUNS
1. 'Visual Odometry (Sequence)' folds the whole batch: corners tracked with pyramidal Lucas-Kanade, re-detected only when too few survive; the relative pose of each pair from the 5-point algorithm + RANSAC; each step dead-reckoned onto the running pose. Identical to the three single-step nodes in exercise_visual_odometry.json - it calls the same code - but a per-frame graph loop cannot collect a trajectory, because a foreach fold keeps one accumulator and the pose needs two.
2. SCALE. One camera cannot see how far it moved, only which way. The ground-truth track's consecutive distances are fed in as the step lengths, which is what makes the output metric. Swap in wheel odometry or a known baseline for a real deployment; with 'constant' the shape survives and the size is arbitrary.
3. 'Trajectory Error (ATE / RPE)' aligns the estimate onto the truth with a similarity transform - two odometry runs live in their own frames, so comparing raw coordinates would measure that choice, not the estimate - and reports the absolute and relative errors.

WHAT TO LOOK AT
The plot: the grey path is the truth, the ramped one is the estimate, walking dark-to-light from its first frame to its last. Both share ONE world-to-pixel mapping (the same 'extent_from'), so their sizes are comparable; the grid, the metre ticks and the scale bar say how big the error actually is. Small x marks are frames where no pose could be recovered and the previous one was HELD - at this drive's traffic lights the car stands still, and a stationary camera has no parallax, so there is nothing to recover. That is a correct answer, not a failure.
The charts: per-frame error shows WHERE the drift happened (watch the turns), and the surviving-track count is the health signal that precedes it.

Measured on the default drive (447 frames, 333 m): ATE rmse 5.5 m, RPE rmse 0.09 m, 383/447 steps kept. The published reference this is modelled on (alishobeiri/Monocular-Video-Odometery, linked in the 'Data sources' note) scores 13.9 m / 0.46 m on the same decoded frames.

widgets_values:
### Data sources

**Clip + ground truth** — KITTI raw drive `2011_09_26_drive_0009`
(`2011_09_26_drive_0009_sync.zip` and `2011_09_26_calib.zip`):

- [KITTI raw data — downloads, format and licence](https://www.cvlibs.net/datasets/kitti/raw_data.php)
- Licence: [CC BY-NC-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0/) — **non-commercial**
- [Geiger et al., *Vision meets Robotics: The KITTI Dataset*](https://www.cvlibs.net/publications/Geiger2013IJRR.pdf) — cite this if you publish

The pack ships the derived pose file (`example_inputs/kitti_2011_09_26_drive_0009_poses.txt`), so it carries KITTI's **non-commercial** licence too. The clip itself is 48 MB and is not shipped - the note beside this one says how to encode it from `2011_09_26_drive_0009_sync.zip`.

**Reference implementation** scored against in the note beside this one:

- [alishobeiri/Monocular-Video-Odometery](https://github.com/alishobeiri/Monocular-Video-Odometery)
